newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish president approves anti-Islamist coalition.
newsitem.headline: Turkish president approves anti-Islamist coalition.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel on Monday approved an anti-Islamist coalition government led by Mesut Yilmaz after months of political uncertainty, the president's office said.
"The president...approved the Turkish republic's 55th government, under the leadership of Mesut Yilmaz," Demirel's office said in a statement.
Secularist Yilmaz's government is a minority coalition of three parties that is supported by a fourth parliamentary grouping. Yilmaz has urged early polls next spring.
Yilmaz must now face a confidence vote in parliament within around 10 days. A wave of resignations from an opposing conservative party has given him an apparent majority in the 550-member assembly.
The government is being set up to prevent the Islamists of outgoing caretaker Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan from returning to power.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, resigned two weeks ago under pressure from the secularist army.

Stocks in Istanbul ended the morning session more than four percent higher on hopes that Yilmaz would establish a solid government to end political uncertainty generated by a dispute between the outgoing Islamist-led government and the secularist establishment.
